RESULT the theorem's right-hand side is `False`, so the goal reduces to exhibiting a nonzero continuous `f` with every unit-sphere integral zero.

FACT the candidate `f(x) = sin(π‖x‖)/‖x‖` (value π at 0) is continuous and nonzero.

FACT for `|c| = s`, the sphere integral of a radial `g(|x|)` reduces to `(2π/s) ∫_{|s-1|}^{s+1} t·g(t) dt`. With `g(t) = sin(πt)/t` this integral is `(cos(π|s-1|) - cos(π(s+1)))/π = 0`, so the candidate passes the hypothesis mathematically.

FACT the Lean proof would need to compute `∫ x in sphere C 1, f x ∂μH[2]` for every center `C` in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`. That requires a spherical-coordinate change of variables for the 2-dimensional Hausdorff measure on a sphere.

FACT I searched the installed compiled Mathlib for Hausdorff-measure results mentioning spheres and found none, so that computation is not available from the library.

HYP building that computation from scratch is out of reach here, and no `sorry`-free shortcut exists: any nonzero `f` killing all unit spheres needs exactly this integral identity.

I give up. The statement is false, so `False` is the correct right-hand side and the counterexample above is the right witness, but I cannot finish the formal proof of the sphere-integral identity with the available Mathlib. The file `/work/putnam_2019_a4.lean` is unchanged.
